title: How Meta ads really work, and what a sale is worth to you

say: How Meta ads really work, and what a sale is worth to you.
This is the video for module one of Paid Advertising with Meta Ads.
Boosting is a shortcut. Ads Manager is the full workshop. Every ad lives in three levels. The campaign sets the objective, the result Meta should find for you.

say: Each time someone opens Facebook or Instagram, Meta holds an instant auction. The winner is not simply the highest payer. It combines three things. First, your bid.

panel.heading: How Meta picks which ad to show

cards.d: What you will pay for a result. With Highest volume, Meta sets it from your budget.
How likely this person is to click, message or buy.
Feedback such as hiding the ad, and low-quality tricks like engagement bait.

say: Second, how likely this person is to do what you asked.

say: Third, ad quality. So a relevant ad that people respond to wins more auctions, and each result costs less. A dull or misleading ad pays more.

say: When an ad set starts, Meta explores who responds. This is the learning phase, and results jump around.

say: Changing targeting, creative or the event, or a large budget change, sends it back. So plan properly, launch, and leave it alone, unless a link is wrong or an ad is rejected.

say: Meta's guidance is about 50 events in 7 days to exit learning. Amaka ran 9 tiny campaigns at 2,000 naira a day, so none could get there. She merged them into one Sales campaign at 18,000 naira a day, with her 5 best ads inside.

panel.rule: About 50 optimisation events in 7 days to exit learning.

say: The objective tells Meta whom to look for. Choose Traffic, and Meta finds people who click. Choose Sales, and it finds people who buy. Often they are different people.
Funmi spends about 35,000 naira on each ad set. The Traffic one gets clicks for just 25 naira, but only 4 purchases.
The Sales one costs more per click, yet brings 11 purchases. Return on ad spend, ROAS, is 5.66 against 2.06. So judge on cost per result and ROAS. Use the cheap numbers only to diagnose why.
Advanced advertisers do the maths before they open Ads Manager. Without a target, you cannot tell if a sale at 4,000 naira is excellent or ruinous.
Kemi's products, packaging, payment fee and delivery subsidy cost 9,070 naira per order.

What is left, 8,930 naira, is the most she can spend to win one order and break even. That is her break-even cost per acquisition, or CPA. Her margin is about 49.6 percent, so her break-even ROAS is about 2.0.
She aims lower, at 5,400 naira, so the business makes real profit. Below ROAS 2.0 she pauses or fixes. Above 3.3 she considers scaling.

If 20 percent of orders are refused at the door, each order is worth only 80 percent of what Meta reports. Meta cannot see WhatsApp sales, so record those yourself. Confirm your card works before launch.
Never let a client borrow for ad spend on a hoped-for ROAS. And scammers send fake policy violation messages. Never enter your password from a link, and turn on two-factor authentication.

panel.heading: Nigerian realities and safety
items: Count delivered orders, not placed ones
Track WhatsApp orders yourself
Test your payment card before launch
Never borrow for ad spend
Ignore policy messages with links; use 2FA

say: To remember. One campaign per goal, with a few well-funded ad sets. Relevance and quality win the auction. Give an ad set room for about 50 events in 7 days. Judge on cost per result and ROAS. And know your break-even CPA before you spend a single naira.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One campaign per goal; few, funded ad sets
Relevance and quality win the auction
About 50 events in 7 days to learn
Judge on cost per result and ROAS
Break-even CPA is gross profit per order

say: Now practise. Map an account and redraw it with fewer ad sets. Calculate a real report by hand. Then build a unit economics sheet with your break-even CPA, target CPA and the event your budget can support.
